The State can impose reasonable restrictions on the exercise of the freedom of speech and expression on the grounds of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the state, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, and incitement to an offence. Freedom of Assembly Every citizen has the right to assemble peaceably and without arms. It includes the right to hold public meetings, demonstrations and take out processions. This freedom can be exercised only on public land and the assembly must be peaceful and unarmed. This provision does not protect violent, disorderly, riotous assemblies, or one that causes breach of public peace or one that involves arms. This right does not include the right to strike. The State can impose reasonable restrictions on the exercise of right of assembly on two grounds, namely, sovereignty and integrity of India and public order including the maintenance of traffic in the area concerned. Under Section 144 of Criminal Procedure Code (1973), a magistrate can restrain an assembly, meeting or procession if there is a risk of obstruction, annoyance or danger to human life, health or safety or a disturbance of the public tranquillity or a riot or any affray. Under Section 141 of the Indian Penal Code, as assembly of five or more persons becomes unlawful if the object is
options: (a) to resist the execution of any law or legal process;
(b) to forcibly occupy the property of some person;
(c) to commit any mischief or criminal trespass;

(d) to force some person to do an illegal act; and (e) to threaten the government or its officials on exercising lawful powers. Freedom of Association All citizens have the right to form associations or unions or co-operative societies10b. It includes the right to form political parties, companies, partnership firms, societies, clubs, organisations, trade unions or any body of persons. It not only includes the right to start an association or union but also to continue with the association or union as such. Further, it covers the negative right of not to form or join an association or union. Reasonable restrictions can be imposed on the exercise of this right by the State on the grounds of sovereignty and integrity of India, public order and morality. Subject to these restrictions, the citizens have complete liberty to form associations or unions for pursuing lawful objectives and purposes. However, the right to obtain recognition of the association is not a fundamental right. The Supreme Court held that the trade unions have no guaranteed right to effective bargaining or right to strike or right to declare a lock-out. The right to strike can be controlled by an appropriate industrial law. Freedom of Movement This freedom entitles every citizen to move freely throughout the territory of the country. He can move freely from one state to another or from one place to another within a state. This right underline the idea that India is one unit so far as the citizens are concerned. (iii) Both, the Parliament and state legislature can make laws with respect to any of the matters

enumerated in the Concurrent List. This list has at present 52 subjects (originally 473 subjects) like criminal law and procedure, civil procedure, marriage and divorce, population control and family planning, electricity, labour wel-fare, economic and social planning, drugs, newspapers, books and printing press, and others. The power to make laws with respect to residuary subjects (i.e., the matters which are not enumerated in any of the three lists) is vested in the Parliament. This residuary power of legisla-tion includes the power to levy residuary taxes. From the above scheme, it is clear that the matters of national importance and the matters which requires uniformity of legislation nationwide are included in the Union List. The matters of regional and local importance and the matters which permits diversity of interest are specified in the State List. The matters on which uniformity of legislation throughout the country is desirable but not essential are enumerated in the concurrent list. Thus, it permits diversity along with uniformity. In US, only the powers of the Federal Government are enumerated in the Constitution and the residuary powers are left to the states. The Australian Constitution followed the American pattern of single enumeration of powers. In Canada, on the other hand, there is a double enumeration Federal and Provincial, and the residuary powers are vested in the Centre. The Government of India (GoI) Act of 1935 provided for a three-fold emumenration, viz., federal, provincial and concurrent.  The residuary power of taxation (that is, the power to impose taxes not enumerated in any of the three lists) is vested in the Parliament. Under this provision, the Parliament has imposed gift tax, wealth tax and expenditure tax. The Constitution also draws a distinction between the power to levy and collect a tax and the power to appropriate the proceeds of the tax so levied and collected. For example, the income-tax is levied and collected by the Centre but its proceeds are distributed between the Centre and the states. Further, the Constitution has placed the following restrictions on the taxing powers of the states: (i) A state legislature can impose taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments. But, the total amount of such taxes payable by any person should not exceed Rs. 2,500 per annum.15 (ii) A state legislature can impose taxes on the sale or purchase of goods (other than newspapers). But, this power of the states to impose sales tax is subjected to the four restrictions:
options: (a) no tax can be imposed on the sale or purchase taking place outside the states;
(b) no tax can be imposed on the sale or purchase taking place in the course of import or export;
(c) no tax can be imposed on the sale or purchase taking place in the course of inter-state trade and commerce; and

(d) a tax imposed on the sale or purchase of goods declared by Parliament to be of special importance in inter-state trade and commerce is subject to the restrictions and conditions specified by the Parliament.16 (iii) A state legislature can impose tax on the consumption or sale of electricity. But, no tax can be imposed on the consumption or sale of electricity which is (a) consumed by the Centre or sold to the Centre; or (b) consumed in the construction, maintenance or operation of any railway by the Centre or by the concerned railway company or sold to the Centre or the railway company for the same purpose. (iv) A state legislature can impose a tax in respect of any water or electricity stored, generated, consumed, distributed or sold by any authority established by Parliament for regulating or developing any inter-state river or river valley. But, such a law, to be effective, should be reserved for the president s consideration and receive his assent.

subject: Geography
stem: Turkey is located between
options: (c) Gulf of Suez and Mediterranean Sea
(d) Gulf of Aqaba and Dead Se
trapAnalysis:
Turkey is a transcontinental country located between the Black Sea (to the north) and the Mediterranean Sea (to the south). The western part (Thrace) is in Europe; the eastern part (Anatolia/Asia Minor) is in Asia, separated by the Bosphorus Strait, Sea of Marmara, and Dardanelles.

**Why others are wrong:**

(a) Black Sea and Caspian Sea — the Caspian Sea is much further east (bordered by Iran, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, Russia). Turkey doesn't touch it.

(c) Gulf of Suez — that's in Egypt (Sinai Peninsula).

(d) Gulf of Aqaba and Dead Sea — those are between Israel, Jordan, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia. Key geographic fact: Turkey controls the strategically vital Turkish Straits (Bosphorus + Dardanelles) connecting the Black Sea to the Mediterranean.

subject: Geography
stem:
What are the benefits of implementing the 'Integrated Watershed Development Programme?

1. Prevention of soil runoff
2. Linking the country's perennial rivers with seasonal rivers
3. Rainwater harvesting and recharge of groundwater table
4. Regeneration of natural vegetation

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
trapAnalysis:
Benefits of Integrated Watershed Development Programme (IWDP):

(1) Prevention of soil runoff — CORRECT: The primary goal of watershed management is to reduce soil erosion by building check dams, contour bunding, and vegetative barriers.

(2) Linking perennial and seasonal rivers — WRONG: River interlinking is a completely separate mega-project (National River Linking Project). IWDP has nothing to do with it. This is the distractor.

(3) Rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge — CORRECT: Watershed development includes building percolation tanks, farm ponds, and recharge structures to capture rainwater and replenish groundwater.

(4) Regeneration of natural vegetation — CORRECT: Afforestation and pasture development are key components, which help restore natural vegetation cover. Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct. Remember: Watershed = localised water and soil conservation, NOT large-scale river engineering.

subject: History
stem: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was
options: (a) the mosque for the use of Royal Family
(c) the hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars of various religions.
(d) the room in which the nobles belonging in different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs.
trapAnalysis:
Ibadat Khana ('House of Worship') was a hall built by Akbar in 1575 at Fatehpur Sikri specifically for religious discussions and debates. Akbar invited scholars from different religions — Islam, Hinduism, Christianity, Jainism, Zoroastrianism — to discuss and debate their faiths. This exposure eventually led Akbar to create 'Din-i-Ilahi' (a syncretic faith).

**Key distinction:**

(a) It was NOT a mosque.

(b) It was NOT Akbar's private prayer room.

(d) It was NOT just for nobles — it was for scholars of various religions invited by Akbar.

(Ref: NCERT Class 7, Our Pasts-II, p.54)

subject: History
stem: Every year, a month long ecologically important campaign/festival is held during which certain communities/tribes plant samplings of fruit-bearing trees. Which of the following are such communities/tribes ?
trapAnalysis: The Gond and Korku tribes of central India (Madhya Pradesh region) celebrate a month-long traditional eco-festival where they plant saplings of fruit-bearing trees. This is their own green revolution — a conservation practice passed down through generations, rooted in their deep relationship with forests. The other pairs (Bhutia-Lepcha from Sikkim, Irula-Toda from Nilgiris, Sahariya-Agariya from MP/UP) are not associated with this specific tree-planting festival.

subject: History
stem: Chaitra 1 of the national calendar based on the Saka Era corresponds to which one of the following dates of the Gregorian calendar in a normal year of 365 days ?
trapAnalysis:
India's national calendar is based on the Saka Era (starting year: 78 AD). Chaitra is the first month. Chaitra 1 falls on: 22nd March in a normal year (365 days), 21st March in a leap year (366 days). This is easy to remember: India's financial year also starts close to this date (1st April). The Saka calendar was adopted in 1957 along with the Gregorian calendar for official purposes.

(Ref: India Year Book)

trapAnalysis:
**Pair 1** — CORRECT: Tabo Monastery (founded 996 AD) is in Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh. It's called the 'Ajanta of the Himalayas' for its ancient murals.

**Pair 2** — WRONG: Lhotsava Lhakhang is in Nako village, Kinnaur district (Himachal Pradesh), NOT Zanskar Valley. 'Lhotsava' refers to the great translator Rinchen Zangpo who built it.

**Pair 3** — CORRECT: Alchi Temple Complex is in Ladakh. It's famous for its stunning 11th-century Buddhist art and is one of the oldest surviving monastery complexes in Ladakh.

**Memory aid:** Tabo → Spiti, Alchi → Ladakh, Lhotsava Lhakhang → Nako/Kinnaur (not Zanskar).

subject: History
stem: With reference to India's culture and tradition, what is 'Kalaripayattu'?
options: (a) It is an ancient Bhakti cult of Shaivism still prevalent in some parts of South India.
(b) It is an ancient style bronze and brasswork still found in southern part of Coromandel area.
(c) It is an ancient form of dance-drama and a living tradition in the northern part of Malabar.
(d) It is an ancient martial art and a living tradition in some parts of South India.
trapAnalysis:
Kalaripayattu is one of the oldest martial arts in the world, originating in Kerala (South India). 'Kalari' = training ground/gymnasium, 'Payattu' = fight/exercise. It includes strikes, kicks, weapons training (swords, shields, spears), and knowledge of vital pressure points (marma). It is still practised as a living tradition in Kerala and parts of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

**Why other options are wrong:**

(a) It's not a Bhakti/Shaivism cult.

(b) It's not metalwork/bronze casting.

(c) It's not a dance-drama — Kathakali is the dance-drama from the same region.

subject: History
stem:
Consider the following languages :

1. Gujarati
2. Kannada
3. Telugu

Which of the above has/have been declared as 'Classical Language/Languages' by the Government ?
trapAnalysis:
As of the 2014 question, Kannada and Telugu had been declared Classical Languages by the Government. Gujarati was NOT on the list. The Classical Language status (as of 2014): Tamil

(2004) , Sanskrit

(2005) , Kannada

(2008) , Telugu

(2008) , Malayalam

(2013) , Odia

(2014) . Gujarati, despite being an ancient language, did not receive this status. Criteria for Classical Language status include: high antiquity (1500+ years), ancient literature, original literary tradition not borrowed from another language.

**Note:** In 2024, Marathi, Bengali, Pali, Prakrit, and Assamese were also granted Classical Language status, but that's after this question was asked.

subject: History
stem:
With reference to the famous Sattriya dance, consider the following statements :

1. Sattriya is a combination of music, dance and drama
2. It is a centuries-old living tradition of Vaishnavites of Assam
3. It is based on classical Ragas and Talas of devotional songs composed by Tulsidas, Kabir and Mirabai

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
trapAnalysis:
Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam, recognised by Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

**Key facts:**

**Statement 1** — CORRECT: It combines music, dance, and drama (like most Indian classical forms).

**Statement 2** — CORRECT: It is a centuries-old Vaishnavite tradition, practised in 'Sattras' (Vaishnavite monasteries) of Assam, founded by the saint Srimanta Sankardeva (15th century).

**Statement 3** — WRONG: The music is based on 'Borgeets' (devotional songs composed by Sankardeva and Madhavdeva), NOT by Tulsidas, Kabir, or Mirabai — those saints belong to the North Indian Bhakti tradition.

**Trap alert:** UPSC mixes up Bhakti saints from different regions.

subject: Economy
stem:
With reference to Union Budget, which of the following is/are covered under Non-Plan Expenditure ?

1. Defence expenditure
2. Interest payments
3. Salaries and pensions
4. Subsidies

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
In the old budget classification (before 2017 when Plan/Non-Plan distinction was abolished), Non-Plan Expenditure covered all recurring, committed spending that the government must pay regardless of development plans:

(1) Defence expenditure — salaries, equipment, operations.

(2) Interest payments — on government borrowings.

(3) Salaries and pensions — of government employees.

(4) Subsidies — food, fertilizer, fuel. All four are correct. Think of Non-Plan as 'maintenance spending' — the government has no choice but to pay these. Plan Expenditure was for new development projects under Five-Year Plans.

(Ref: NCERT Economics, Uma Kapila)

subject: Environment
stem:
Consider the following statements :

1. Animal Welfare Board of India is established under the Environment (Protection) Act,
1986. 
2. National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body
3. National Ganga River Basin Authority is chaired by the Prime Minister

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
trapAnalysis:
**Statement 1** — WRONG: Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) was established under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 — NOT the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. This is a common UPSC trick — mixing up the parent Act.

**Statement 2** — CORRECT: NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority) IS a statutory body, created by amending the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 in 2006. It oversees Project Tiger.

**Statement 3** — CORRECT: NGRBA (National Ganga River Basin Authority) was chaired by the Prime Minister. It was set up in 2009 under the Environment (Protection) Act. (Later replaced by National Mission for Clean Ganga in 2016.)

subject: Environment
stem:
Which of the following adds/ads carbon dioxide to the carbon cycle on the planet Earth ?

1. Volcanic action
2. Respiration
3. Photosynthesis
4. Decay of organic matter

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
The question asks what ADDS CO2 to the atmosphere:

(1) Volcanic action — CORRECT: Volcanoes release massive amounts of CO2 trapped in the Earth's interior.

(2) Respiration — CORRECT: All living organisms (plants, animals, microbes) take in O2 and release CO2 during respiration.

(3) Photosynthesis — WRONG: Photosynthesis does the OPPOSITE — it REMOVES CO2 from the atmosphere and converts it into glucose using sunlight. Plants absorb CO2, not release it.

(4) Decay of organic matter — CORRECT: Decomposition of dead organisms by bacteria and fungi releases CO2 back into the atmosphere. Memory trick: Photosynthesis is the only process that TAKES CO2 OUT. Volcanoes, respiration, decay, and burning fossil fuels all ADD CO2.

(Ref: NCERT Class 11 Geography, Ch.15)

subject: Environment
stem: Among the following organisms, which one does not belong to the class of other three ?
trapAnalysis:
This is a classification question. Mite, Scorpion, and Spider all belong to Class Arachnida (8 legs, no antennae, body divided into cephalothorax and abdomen). Crab belongs to Class Crustacea (10 legs, two pairs of antennae, hard exoskeleton). So Crab is the odd one out.

**Quick identification trick:** Count the legs — Arachnids = 8 legs, Insects = 6 legs, Crustaceans = usually 10 legs. But beyond leg count, crabs breathe through gills and live in water/moist environments, while arachnids are mostly terrestrial and breathe through book lungs or tracheae.

subject: Environment
stem:
Which of the following are some important pollutants released by steel industry in India ?

1. Oxides of sulphur
2. Oxide of nitrogen
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Carbon dioxide

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Steel-making involves burning coke (coal) at very high temperatures and processing iron ore — this releases ALL four pollutants:

(1) Oxides of sulphur (SOx) — from sulphur in coal/ore,

(2) Oxides of nitrogen (NOx) — from high-temperature combustion,

(3) Carbon monoxide (CO) — from incomplete combustion of coke,

(4) Carbon dioxide (CO2) — from complete combustion. Whenever UPSC asks about pollutants from heavy industry, 'all of the above' is usually correct because these processes are inherently dirty.

subject: Environment
stem:
Consider the following pairs:

| | Wetland | Confluence of rivers |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Harike Wetlands | Confluence of Beas and Satluj/Sutlej |
| 2. | Keoladeo Ghana National Park | Confluence of Banas and Chambal |
| 3. | Kolleru Lake | Confluence of Musi and Krishna |

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
trapAnalysis:
Only Pair 1 is correct: Harike Wetland — CORRECT: Located at the confluence of Beas and Sutlej rivers in Punjab. A barrage was built here in 1952, creating the Harike Lake. It's a Ramsar site and an important habitat for migratory birds. Keoladeo Ghana NP — WRONG pairing: It is near Bharatpur (Rajasthan) and is fed by the Ajan Bund (a man-made reservoir). It is NOT at the Banas-Chambal confluence. The Banas joins Chambal much further south. Kolleru Lake — WRONG pairing: It lies between the Krishna and Godavari river deltas in Andhra Pradesh, NOT at the Musi-Krishna confluence. The Musi is a tributary of Krishna that flows through Hyderabad.

**Tip:** For wetland questions, learn the river association and state of each Ramsar site.

subject: Environment
stem: If a wetland of international importance is brought under the 'Montreux Record', what does it imply ?
options: (a) Changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur in the wetland as a result of human interference.
(b) The country in which the wetland is located should enact a low to prohibit any human activity within five kilometres from the edge of the wetland.
(c) The survival of the wetland depends on the cultural practices and traditions of certain communities living in its vicinity and therefore the cultural diversity therein should not be destroyed.
(d) It is given the status of 'World Heritage Site'.
trapAnalysis:
The Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar wetland sites where ecological changes have occurred, are occurring, or are likely to occur due to human interference. Think of it as a 'red flag list' or 'danger list' for wetlands. Being on the Montreux Record means the wetland needs urgent attention and conservation measures. It does NOT mean:

(b) A 5 km no-activity zone is created — no such rule exists.

(c) Cultural diversity protection — this confuses it with UNESCO cultural heritage concepts.

(d) World Heritage Site status — that's a separate UNESCO designation. India's Montreux Record sites have included Chilika Lake (removed after improvement), Loktak Lake, and Keoladeo Ghana NP.

subject: Environment
stem:
If you walk through countryside, you are likely to see some birds stalking alongside the cattle to seize the insects disturbed by their movement through grasses. Which one of the following is/are such bird/birds ?

1. Painted Stork
2. Common Myna
3. Black-necked Crane

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis: Only the Common Myna follows cattle. The Common Myna (also called the Indian Myna) is a classic example of 'commensalism' — it walks alongside grazing cattle and picks up insects (grasshoppers, beetles) that get disturbed as cattle move through the grass. The cattle are neither helped nor harmed. Painted Stork — a large wading bird found near wetlands and marshes, NOT alongside cattle in grasslands. It feeds on fish in shallow water. Black-necked Crane — a rare, high-altitude bird found in Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh wetlands. It lives in remote marshes, not in farmland alongside cattle. The Cattle Egret is another bird famous for this behaviour, but it wasn't in the options.

subject: Environment
stem:
With reference to a conservation organization called 'Wetlands International', which of the following statements is/are correct ?

1. It is an intergovernmental organizatioin formed by the countries which are signatories to Ramsar Convention
2. It works at the field level to develop and mobilize knowledge, and use the practical experience to advocate for better policies

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
**Statement 1** — WRONG: Wetlands International is a global NGO (non-governmental organisation), NOT an intergovernmental organisation. It was not formed by Ramsar Convention signatories. It's an independent body headquartered in the Netherlands that works on wetland conservation worldwide.

**Don't confuse it with the Ramsar Convention Secretariat (which IS intergovernmental).

**Statement 2** — CORRECT:** Wetlands International works at the field level — conducting on-ground research, building knowledge, and using that practical experience to advocate for better wetland policies with governments. Key distinction for UPSC: NGO (non-governmental, civil society) vs IGO (intergovernmental, formed by governments). Wetlands International = NGO. Ramsar Convention = international treaty/IGO framework.

subject: Environment
stem:
With reference to Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), consider the following statements :

1. It is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Environment and Forests
2. It strives to conserve nature through action-based research, education and public awareness
3. It organizes and conducts nature trails and camps for the general public

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
trapAnalysis:
**Statement 1** — WRONG: BNHS (founded 1883) is one of India's oldest NGOs for nature conservation. It is NOT an autonomous organisation under MoEF&CC. It receives government grants but operates independently. The MoEF lists its autonomous bodies separately (like Wildlife Institute of India, ZSI, BSI, FSI) — BNHS is not among them.

**Statement 2** — CORRECT: BNHS works through action-based research (bird migration studies, endangered species surveys), education, and public awareness campaigns.

**Statement 3** — CORRECT: BNHS organises nature trails, bird-watching trips, camps, and workshops for the general public. It's headquartered in Mumbai's Hornbill House.

**UPSC trap:** Just because an organisation works closely with the government doesn't mean it's an 'autonomous body under' a ministry.

subject: Environment
stem:
With reference to 'Eco-Sensitive Zones', which of the following statements is/are correct ?

1. Eco-Sensitive Zones are the areas that are declared under the Wildlife (Protection) Act,
1972. 
2. The purpose of the declaration of Eco-Sensitive Zones is to prohibit all kinds of human activities in those zones except agriculture

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Both statements are wrong.

**Statement 1** — WRONG: Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs) are declared under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — NOT the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. They are buffer zones around National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.

**Statement 2** — WRONG: ESZs do NOT prohibit ALL human activities. They regulate certain activities (like mining, large industries, major construction) but allow many others (like agriculture, rain-water harvesting, organic farming). The specific prohibitions/regulations vary from zone to zone and are notified individually by MoEF. Think of ESZs as 'transition zones' — not no-go zones.

subject: Environment
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Earth Hour'

1. It is an initiative of UNEP and UNESCO
2. It is a movement in which the participants switch off the lights for one hour on a certain day every year
3. It is a movement to raise the awareness about the climate change and the need to save the planet

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
trapAnalysis:
**Statement 1** — WRONG: Earth Hour is an initiative of WWF (World Wildlife Fund / World Wide Fund for Nature), NOT UNEP or UNESCO. It started in Sydney, Australia in 2007.

**Statement 2** — CORRECT: Participants switch off non-essential lights for one hour (8:30 PM to 9:30 PM local time) on the last Saturday of March every year.

**Statement 3** — CORRECT: The purpose is to raise awareness about climate change and the need for environmental sustainability. It's a symbolic act — the actual energy saved is minimal, but it sparks conversation. Common

**UPSC trap:** mixing up which UN/international body runs which initiative. WWF also runs Earth Overshoot Day and the Living Planet Report.

subject: Environment
stem:
Consider the following international agreements :

1. The international Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture
2. The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
3. The World Heritage Convention

Which of the above has/have a bearing on the biodiversity ?
trapAnalysis:
All three international agreements have a bearing on biodiversity:

(1) International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA) — DIRECTLY about biodiversity; it deals with conservation and sustainable use of plant genetic resources (crop diversity, seed banks).

(2) UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) — land degradation and desertification destroy habitats, so combating it protects biodiversity. UNCCD itself states it 'collaborates closely with the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).'

(3) World Heritage Convention — protects natural World Heritage Sites (like Sundarbans, Western Ghats, Kaziranga), which are biodiversity hotspots. Think broadly: biodiversity is affected by agriculture, land degradation, AND habitat protection — all three conventions address one of these.

subject: Environment
stem: Lichens, which are capable of initiating ecolological succession even on a bare rock, are actually a symbiotic association of
trapAnalysis: Lichens = Algae + Fungi living together (symbiosis/mutualism). The algae (or cyanobacteria) do photosynthesis and make food, while the fungi provide structure, protection, and help retain moisture. This partnership is so tough that lichens can colonise bare rock — making them pioneer species in ecological succession. Remember: it's NOT bacteria, NOT mosses. (NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch.13)

subject: Environment
stem:
Consider the following :

1. Bats
2. Bears
3. Rodents The phenomenon of hibernation can be observed in

which of the above kinds of animals ?
options: (d) Hibernation cannot be observed in any of the above
trapAnalysis:
All three groups hibernate:

(1) Bats — many bat species hibernate during winter in caves or attics. Their heart rate drops from 400 to 25 beats per minute.

(2) Bears — classic hibernators. They enter a state of torpor (slightly different from 'true' hibernation) during winter, living off stored body fat.

(3) Rodents — many rodents hibernate, including ground squirrels, chipmunks, and dormice. Some rodents are among the deepest true hibernators.

**Common misconception:** Some students think only bears hibernate. Actually, many small mammals hibernate more deeply than bears. Bears' body temperature drops only slightly, while small hibernators like ground squirrels can cool to near 0°C. All three are correct.

subject: Environment
stem:
What are the significances of a practical approach to sugarcane production known as 'Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative' ?

1. Seed cost is very low in this compared to the conventional method of cultivation
2. Drip irrigation can be practiced very effectively in this
3. There is no application of chemical/inorganic fertilizers at all in this
4. The scope for intercropping is more in this compared to the conventional method of cultivation

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
The Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative (SSI) is an improved method adapted from SRI (System of Rice Intensification).

**Key features:**

**Statement 1** — CORRECT: SSI uses single-bud chips (settlings) instead of full setts, drastically reducing seed cane cost (only 1/6th of conventional seed material).

**Statement 2** — CORRECT: SSI uses wider spacing (5 ft × 2 ft), which makes drip irrigation very effective and practical.

**Statement 3** — WRONG: SSI encourages REDUCED use of chemical fertilizers and promotes organic inputs, but it does NOT completely eliminate chemical fertilizers. The word 'no application at all' makes this an absolute claim, which is false.

**Statement 4** — CORRECT: The wider spacing allows more intercropping (growing pulses, vegetables between sugarcane rows). UPSC

**tip:** Beware of extreme words like 'no', 'all', 'never', 'completely' — they usually make the statement wrong.

subject: Environment
stem: With reference to 'Global Environment Facility', which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: (a) It serves as financial mechanism for 'Convention on Biological Diversity' and 'United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change'.
(b) It undertakes scientific research on environmental issues at global level.
(c) It is an agency under OECD to facilitate the transfer of technology and funds to underdeveloped countries with specific aim to protect their environment.
trapAnalysis:
Only statement

(a) is correct. GEF (Global Environment Facility) is an independent international financial mechanism that provides grants to developing countries for projects on: biodiversity, climate change, international waters, land degradation, ozone layer, and persistent organic pollutants. It serves as the FINANCIAL MECHANISM for both CBD (Convention on Biological Diversity) and UNFCCC (UN Framework Convention on Climate Change).

**Why others are wrong:**

(b) GEF funds projects — it does NOT conduct scientific research itself. That's the role of bodies like IPCC or UNEP.

(c) GEF is NOT under OECD. It's an independent body with World Bank as a trustee. It involves 183 countries.

(d) Since

(b) is wrong, 'Both

(a) and

(b) ' is also wrong.

subject: History
stem: Which one of the following pairs does not form part of the six systems of Indian Philosophy ?
trapAnalysis:
The six orthodox systems (Shad Darshana) of Indian Philosophy are:

(1) Sankhya and

(2) Yoga (paired),

(3) Nyaya and

(4) Vaisheshika (paired),

(5) Purva Mimamsa and

(6) Uttara Mimamsa/Vedanta (paired). They are called 'orthodox' (astika) because they accept the authority of the Vedas. Lokayata (Charvaka) is a HETERODOX (nastika) materialist philosophy that rejects the Vedas, the soul, and afterlife. It believes only in direct perception. Kapalika is NOT a philosophical system at all — it's a Shaivite tantric sect known for extreme ascetic practices. So Lokayata + Kapalika is the pair that does NOT belong to the six systems. Memorise the three pairs: Sankhya-Yoga, Nyaya-Vaisheshika, Mimamsa-Vedanta.

(Ref: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)

subject: History
stem: With reference to the cultural history of India, the term 'Panchayatan' refers to
trapAnalysis:
Panchayatana is a style of Hindu temple construction where one main shrine (dedicated to the principal deity) is surrounded by four smaller subsidiary shrines at the four corners. The word literally means 'group of five.' It's like a quincunx pattern (one in the centre, four at corners). This style is found in many North Indian Nagara-style temples. Famous examples: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple (Khajuraho), Lakshmana Temple (Khajuraho), Dashavatara Temple (Deogarh).

**Don't confuse with:**

(a) Panchayat (village council),

(b) any religious sect, or

(d) any administrative post. The '-tan' suffix relates to a structural arrangement, not governance.

(Ref: NCERT + CCRT website)

subject: Environment
stem:
With reference to Neem tree, consider the following statements :

1. Neem oil can be used as a pesticide to control the proliferation of some species of insects and mites
2. Neem seeds are used in the manufacture of biofuels and hospital detergents
3. Neem oil has applications in pharmaceutical industry

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
trapAnalysis:
Neem is called the 'village pharmacy' because of its incredibly wide range of uses. All three statements are correct:

(1) Pesticide — Neem oil contains 'azadirachtin,' a natural insecticide effective against 200+ species of insects and mites. Widely used in organic farming.

(2) Biofuel and detergents — Neem seed oil can be processed into biodiesel, and neem-based hospital-grade detergents/soaps are used for their antiseptic properties.

(3) Pharmaceuticals — Neem extracts are used in medicines for skin diseases, diabetes management, dental care, and as anti-inflammatory agents. When UPSC asks about neem, the answer is usually 'all of the above' because neem genuinely has diverse applications.

subject: Geography
stem: The seasonal reversal of winds is the typical characteristic of
trapAnalysis:
Monsoon climate is defined by the seasonal reversal of prevailing winds. In India: Summer (June–September) — winds blow from the Indian Ocean toward land (SW monsoon), bringing heavy rain. Winter (October–February) — winds reverse and blow from land toward the ocean (NE monsoon), mostly dry (except Tamil Nadu coast).

**Why not the others:** Equatorial climate — has no seasonal wind reversal; it's hot and wet year-round with convectional rainfall. Mediterranean climate — has seasonal rainfall variation (dry summers, wet winters) but not due to wind reversal; it's due to shifting pressure belts. The word 'monsoon' itself comes from the Arabic 'mausim' meaning 'season,' referring to this wind reversal.

(Ref: NCERT Class 11 Geography)

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following pairs:

| | National Highway | Cities connected |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | NH4 | Chennai and Hyderabad |
| 2. | NH6 | Mumbai and Kolkata |
| 3. | NH15 | Ahmedabad and Jodhpur |

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
trapAnalysis:
All three pairs are WRONG (answer is 'None'). The old NH numbering (pre-2010 renumbering) was: NH4 — connected Chennai to Thane (via Bangalore, not Hyderabad). NH6 — connected Hajira (near Surat) to Kolkata (not starting from Mumbai). NH15 — ran from Pathankot to Samakhiali (Gujarat), passing through Amritsar and Jaisalmer, NOT connecting Ahmedabad to Jodhpur.

**Note:** India renumbered all National Highways after 2010. The new system uses different numbers entirely. UPSC sometimes tests old NH numbers from pre-2010 NCERT textbooks.

(Ref: NCERT Class 12 Geography Part II)

subject: Geography
stem:
In India, the problem of soil erosion is associated with which of the following ?

1. Terrace cultivation
2. Deforestation
3. Tropical climate

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Only Deforestation causes soil erosion.

(1) Terrace cultivation — WRONG association. Terracing actually PREVENTS soil erosion on hill slopes by creating flat steps that slow down water runoff. It's a soil conservation technique, not a cause of erosion.

(2) Deforestation — CORRECT: Removing trees exposes soil to rain and wind. Tree roots hold soil together; without them, rain washes topsoil away (sheet erosion, gully erosion). This is India's biggest cause of soil erosion.

(3) Tropical climate — WRONG: Having a tropical climate doesn't automatically mean soil erosion. Many tropical regions have dense forests that protect soil. It's deforestation IN tropical areas that causes erosion, not the climate itself. UPSC trick:

**Don't confuse a soil conservation method (terracing) with a cause of erosion.

(Ref:** NCERT Class 11 Geography)

subject: Geography
stem:
Which of the following phenomena might have influenced the evolution of organisms ?

1. Continental drift
2. Glacial cycles

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Both continental drift and glacial cycles have profoundly influenced evolution: Continental drift — as continents moved apart over millions of years, populations of organisms got isolated on different landmasses. This geographic isolation led to independent evolution (e.g., marsupials evolved uniquely in Australia after it separated from other continents). Glacial cycles — repeated ice ages caused habitats to expand, contract, and shift. Species had to adapt, migrate, or go extinct. Glaciation also created land bridges (like the Bering Strait) that allowed species to cross between continents. Both are well-established drivers of evolution. Neither can be excluded.

(Ref: NCERT Class 11 Geography)

subject: Geography
stem:
With reference to 'Changpa' community of India, consider the following statements :

1. They live mainly in the State of Uttarakhand
2. They rear the Pashmina goats that yield a fine wool
3. They are kept in the category of Scheduled Tribes

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
trapAnalysis:
The Changpa are nomadic pastoralists from the Changthang plateau in Ladakh (now a Union Territory, earlier part of J&K).

**Statement 1** — WRONG: They live in Ladakh, NOT Uttarakhand. This is the most common trick in this question.

**Statement 2** — CORRECT: They rear Changra goats (Pashmina goats) that produce the world-famous Pashmina wool — one of the finest and most expensive wools.

**Statement 3** — CORRECT: Changpas are classified as a Scheduled Tribe.

**Memory aid:** Changpa → Changthang → Ladakh → Pashmina.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following pairs:

| | Programme/Project | Ministry |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Drought-Prone Area Programme | Ministry of Agriculture |
| 2. | Desert Development Programme | Ministry of Environment and Forests |
| 3. | National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas | Ministry of Rural Development |

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
trapAnalysis:
All three programme-ministry pairings are WRONG:

(1) Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP) — was under the Ministry of Rural Development, NOT Ministry of Agriculture.

(2) Desert Development Programme (DDP) — was also under the Ministry of Rural Development, NOT Ministry of Environment and Forests.

(3) National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA) — was under the Ministry of Agriculture, NOT Ministry of Rural Development. The trick here is that DPAP and DDP (both area-development programmes) were under Rural Development, while NWDPRA (a farming-related watershed project) was under Agriculture. The question swaps them to confuse. Answer: None.

(Ref: India Year Book)

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following pairs:

| | Region | Well-known for the production of |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Kinnaur | Areca nut |
| 2. | Mewat | Mango |
| 3. | Coromandel | Soya bean |

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
trapAnalysis:
All three pairs are WRONG — a rare 'None' answer.

(1) Kinnaur (Himachal Pradesh) — famous for apples, dry fruits, and chilgoza pine nuts, NOT areca nut. Areca nut grows in warm, tropical coastal regions like Karnataka, Kerala, and Assam.

(2) Mewat (Haryana/Rajasthan border) — an arid/semi-arid region, NOT known for mango. Mango-famous regions include Malihabad (UP), Ratnagiri (Maharashtra), and Malda (West Bengal).

(3) Coromandel (eastern coast of Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh) — known for rice cultivation, NOT soybean. Soybean is grown predominantly in central India — Madhya Pradesh is called the 'Soya State.' When all three pairs are obviously mismatched geographically, answer 'None.'

(Ref: Khullar, India Comprehensive Geography)

subject: Geography
stem:
In the context of food and nutritional security of India, enhancing the 'Seed Replacement Rates' of various crops helps in achieving the food production targets of the future. But what is/are the constraint/constraints in its wider/greater implementation ?

1. There is no National Seeds Policy in place
2. There is no participation of private sector seed companies in the supply of quality seeds of vegetables and planting materials of horticultural crops
3. There is a demand-supply gap regarding quality seeds in case of low value and high volume crops

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Seed Replacement Rate (SRR) = percentage of area sown with certified/quality seeds out of total area sown. Higher SRR means better crop yields. The only real constraint listed here is:

**Statement 1** — WRONG: India DOES have a National Seeds Policy

(2002) .

**Statement 2** — WRONG: Private seed companies ARE active in supplying vegetable seeds and horticultural planting material (companies like Monsanto, Syngenta, Mahyco etc.).

**Statement 3** — CORRECT: The actual bottleneck is for low-value, high-volume crops (like pulses, oilseeds, coarse cereals). Since profit margins are low, private companies avoid these crops, and government production can't meet demand — creating a supply gap.

subject: Geography
stem:
If you travel through the Himalayas, you are likely to see which of the following plants naturally growing there ?

1. Oak
2. Rhododendron
3. Sandalwood

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis: All three grow in the Himalayas, just at different altitudes. Oak and Rhododendron are well-known montane species (temperate/alpine zones). The tricky part is Sandalwood — most students associate it with South India, but sandalwood also grows in the Himalayan foothills in the moist deciduous forests (areas receiving 100–200 cm rainfall). These foothill forests include teak, sal, shisham, and sandalwood. So all three are correct. (NCERT Class 11 Physical Geography, pp.59-60)

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following pairs:

| | Protected Area / Peak | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Dampa Tiger Reserve | Mizoram |
| 2. | Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary | Sikkim |
| 3. | Saramati Peak | Nagaland |

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
trapAnalysis:
**Pair 1** — CORRECT: Dampa Tiger Reserve is in Mizoram (western Mizoram, near the Bangladesh border). It's one of the largest wildlife reserves in the North-East.

**Pair 2** — WRONG: Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary is in Tripura, NOT Sikkim. It is located around the Dumbur Lake (Gumti river reservoir) in Tripura. Sikkim's protected areas include Khangchendzonga NP and Fambong Lho WLS.

**Pair 3** — CORRECT: Saramati Peak (3,841 m) is the highest peak of Nagaland, located on the Nagaland-Myanmar border. It is the highest peak in the Naga Hills.

**Memory tip for NE India:** Learn one key protected area and one key peak per state — UPSC loves NE geography.

subject: Geography
stem:
What is the correct sequence of occurrence of the following cities in South-East Asia as one proceeds from south to north?

1. Bangkok
2. Hanoi
3. Jakarta
4. Singapore

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
trapAnalysis: South to North latitudinal order: Jakarta (6°S — Southern Hemisphere, the southernmost) → Singapore (1°N — almost on the Equator) → Bangkok (14°N) → Hanoi (21°N — the northernmost). So the sequence is 3-4-1-2. How to remember: Jakarta is BELOW the equator (south of it). Singapore is right AT the equator. Bangkok is in the tropics. Hanoi is the farthest north, close to the Tropic of Cancer. Common mistake: Students confuse Singapore and Jakarta. Singapore feels more 'developed/modern' so they assume it's further north, but Jakarta is actually further SOUTH (below the equator). Always verify with a mental map.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following towns of India :

1. Bhadrachalam
2. Chanderi
3. Kancheepuram
4. Karnal

Which of the above are famous for the production of traditional sarees/fabric ?
trapAnalysis:
Only Chanderi and Kancheepuram are famous textile centres: Chanderi (Madhya Pradesh) — known for Chanderi sarees/fabric made of silk and cotton, with fine texture and light weight. Recognised as a GI-tagged product. Kancheepuram (Tamil Nadu) — famous for heavy silk sarees with rich zari work, considered among India's finest wedding sarees. Bhadrachalam (Telangana) — famous for the Rama temple on the banks of Godavari, NOT for textiles. Karnal (Haryana) — known for the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), NOT textiles.

**Tip:** For UPSC, maintain a list of GI-tagged textile products and their locations.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following rivers :

1. Barak
2. Lohit
3. Subansiri

which of the above flows/flow through Arunachal Pradesh ?
trapAnalysis: Rivers flowing through Arunachal Pradesh: Lohit — CORRECT: Flows through eastern Arunachal Pradesh; one of the major tributaries of the Brahmaputra. It enters India at Kibithu. Subansiri — CORRECT: The largest tributary of Brahmaputra, flows through central Arunachal Pradesh. The controversial Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project is located at the Arunachal-Assam border. Barak — WRONG: The Barak River flows through Manipur and southern Assam (Barak Valley), NOT through Arunachal Pradesh. It eventually flows into Bangladesh and becomes the Surma and Kushiyara rivers. Memory: Arunachal's major rivers (west to east) = Kameng, Subansiri, Siang (main Brahmaputra), Dibang, Lohit. Barak is a separate river system altogether.

subject: Geography
stem:
Consider the following pairs:

| | Hills | Region |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Cardamom Hills | Coromandel Coast |
| 2. | Kaimur Hills | Konkan Coast |
| 3. | Mahadeo Hills | Central India |
| 4. | Mikir Hills | North-East India |

Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
trapAnalysis:
**Pair 1** — WRONG: Cardamom Hills are in Kerala/Tamil Nadu (Western Ghats), NOT on the Coromandel Coast. The Coromandel Coast is the eastern coast of South India (Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh).

**Pair 2** — WRONG: Kaimur Hills are in the Vindhyan Range (Bihar/UP/MP — central-eastern India), NOT on the Konkan Coast. The Konkan Coast is the western coast of Maharashtra/Goa/Karnataka.

**Pair 3** — CORRECT: Mahadeo Hills (part of the Satpura Range) are in Central India (Madhya Pradesh). Pachmarhi, India's famous hill station, is in the Mahadeo Hills.

**Pair 4** — CORRECT: Mikir Hills (also called Karbi Anglong Hills) are in North-East India (Assam). The Karbi Anglong district is named after these hills. Pairs 3 and 4 are correct.

(Ref: NCERT Class 11)

subject: Economy
stem:
With reference to Balance of Payments, which of the following constitutes/ constitute the Current Account ?

1. Balance of trade
2. Foreign assets
3. Balance of invisibles
4. Special Drawing Rights

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
The Current Account in Balance of Payments has two main parts:

(1) Balance of Trade — value of goods exported minus imported (visible trade).

(2) Balance of Invisibles — services (IT, tourism), remittances (money sent by Indians abroad), and income (interest/dividends). Foreign assets and SDRs (Special Drawing Rights) belong to the Capital/Financial Account or Reserves, NOT the Current Account. Simple trick: Current Account = day-to-day transactions (trade + services + transfers). Capital Account = assets, investments, and borrowings.

(Ref: NCERT Economics, Uma Kapila)

subject: General Studies
stem: Recently, a series of uprisings of people referred to as 'Arab Spring' originally started from
trapAnalysis:
The Arab Spring began in Tunisia in December 2010 when a street vendor named Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire in protest against police corruption. This triggered mass protests that overthrew President Ben Ali (who fled to Saudi Arabia in January 2011). The movement then spread to Egypt (Mubarak ousted), Libya (Gaddafi killed), Syria (civil war), Yemen, and Bahrain.

**Key point:** Tunisia was the origin, Egypt was the most famous domino to fall.

subject: Economy
stem: The terms 'Marginal Standing Facility Rate' and 'Net Demand and Time Liabilities', sometimes appearing in news, are used in relation to
options: (d) supply and demand of agricultural products
trapAnalysis: Both terms are RBI/banking jargon: MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) — an emergency overnight borrowing window where banks can borrow from RBI at a rate higher than the repo rate (up to 1% of their NDTL). Introduced in May 2011. NDTL (Net Demand and Time Liabilities) — essentially the total deposits and borrowings of a bank (demand deposits like savings/current accounts + time deposits like FDs). CRR and SLR are calculated as a percentage of NDTL. These have zero connection to communications, military, or agriculture.

subject: Economy
stem: The main objective of the 12th Five-Year Plan is
options: (c) sustainable and inclusive growth to reduce unemployment
(d) faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth.
trapAnalysis: The 12th Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) had the theme: 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth.' All three words matter — Faster (higher GDP growth), Sustainable (environmentally responsible), More Inclusive (benefits reaching all sections). The other options miss one or more keywords. UPSC often tests exact official phrasing — so memorise the tagline of each Five-Year Plan. For comparison: 11th Plan = 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth' (no 'sustainable').

subject: Polity
stem: The power to increase the number of judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in
trapAnalysis:
Article 124

(1) says the Supreme Court shall consist of a Chief Justice and such number of other judges as Parliament may by law prescribe. So it is PARLIAMENT that decides the strength of the SC through legislation (like the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act). The President appoints judges but cannot increase the number. The CJI recommends names for appointment but doesn't decide strength. The Law Commission advises on legal reforms but has no such power. Current strength: Originally 8 judges

(1950) , increased multiple times by Parliament — now 34 (including CJI).

(Ref: Laxmikanth)

subject: Economy
stem: In India, cluster bean (Guar) is traditionally used as a vegetable or animal feed, but recently the cultivation of this has assumed significance. Which one of the following statements is correct in this context ?
options: (a) The oil extracted from seeds is used in the manufacture of biodegradable plastics.
(b) The gum made from its seeds is used in the extraction of shale gas
(c) The leaf extract of this plant has the properties of anti-histamines.
(d) It is a source of high quality biodiesel.
trapAnalysis: Guar (cluster bean) suddenly became a high-value crop because guar gum extracted from its seeds is used as a thickening agent in hydraulic fracturing ('fracking') fluid, which is essential for shale gas extraction. When the shale gas boom happened (especially in the USA), demand for guar gum skyrocketed, and India — being the world's largest producer of guar (mainly Rajasthan) — benefited hugely. The other options are fictional uses invented to mislead: guar is not used for biodegradable plastics, anti-histamines, or biodiesel.

subject: Economy
stem: If the interest rate is decreased in an economy, it will
options: (a) decrease the consumption expenditure in the economy
(b) increase the tax collection of the Government.
(c) Increase the investment expenditure in the economy
(d) increase the total savings in the economy.
trapAnalysis:
This is basic macroeconomics (Keynesian theory). When interest rates fall → borrowing becomes cheaper → businesses take more loans → they invest more in factories, equipment, expansion → Investment Expenditure INCREASES.

**Why other options are wrong:**

(a) Consumption may actually increase (not decrease) because EMIs on loans become cheaper.

(b) Tax collection doesn't directly rise just because interest rates fall.

(d) Lower interest rates actually discourage saving (lower returns on FDs/savings accounts), so total savings may fall, not rise.

**Key concept:** Interest rate and investment have an INVERSE relationship.

(Ref: Uma Kapila, Ramesh Singh)

subject: Economy
stem:
In the context of Indian economy which of the following is/are the purpose/purposes of 'Statutory Reserve Requirements'?

1. To enable the Central Bank to control the amount of advances the banks can create
2. To make the people's deposits with banks safe and liquid
3. To prevent the commercial banks from making excessive profits
4. To force the banks to have sufficient vault cash to meet their day-to-day requirements

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Statutory Reserve Requirements (CRR + SLR) serve two main purposes:

(1) Credit control — by locking up a portion of deposits, RBI limits how much money banks can lend out. Higher reserves = less lending = tighter money supply.

(2) Safety and liquidity — reserves ensure banks always have enough funds to honour depositors' withdrawals, preventing bank runs. Why statements 3 and 4 are wrong:

(3) Profit control is NOT the purpose — that's done through competition and regulation, not reserves.

(4) Vault cash for daily use is a bank's own operational decision; CRR is kept WITH the RBI, not in the bank's vault.

(Ref: NCERT Economics)

subject: Economy
stem: The sales tax you pay while purchasing a toothpaste is a
options: (a) Tax imposed by the Central Government
(b) Tax imposed by the central Government but collected by the State Government.
(c) Tax imposed by the State Government but collected by the Central Government.
(d) Tax imposed and collected by the State Government.
trapAnalysis:
Before GST

(2017) , sales tax on goods like toothpaste was under Entry 54 of the State List (Schedule VII). This means the State Government had the power to both impose AND collect it. Easy way to remember: Sales Tax = State (both start with 'S'). The Centre handled excise duty on manufacturing; the State handled sales tax on purchase/sale.

**Note:** After GST, this distinction has changed, but this question is from the pre-GST era.

(Ref: Laxmikanth, D.D. Basu)

subject: Economy
stem: What does venture capital mean ?
options: (a) A short-term capital provided to industries
(b) A long-term start-up capital provided to new entrepreneurs
(c) Funds provided to industries at times of incurring losses.
(d) Funds provided for replacement and renovation of industries.
trapAnalysis:
Venture capital = money given to NEW businesses/startups with high growth potential, in exchange for equity (ownership stake).

**Key features:**

(1) It's long-term, not short-term.

(2) It's for new entrepreneurs, not existing loss-making firms.

(3) It's risk capital — the investor bets on future growth.

**Why other options are wrong:**

(a) Short-term capital = working capital, not venture capital.

(c) Funds for losses = bailout/restructuring.

(d) Replacement/renovation = modernisation loans.

subject: Economy
stem: Which of the following organizations brings out the publication known as 'World Economic Outlook ?
trapAnalysis:
World Economic Outlook (WEO) is published by the IMF (International Monetary Fund), usually twice a year (April and October). It provides analysis of global economic developments and forecasts.

**Don't confuse with other famous publications:** World Bank → World Development Report, UNDP → Human Development Report, WEF (World Economic Forum) → Global Competitiveness Report, Global Risks Report. This is a straightforward factual question — just memorise which organisation publishes which report.

subject: Economy
stem:
Which of the following are associated with 'Planning' in India?

1. The Finance Commission
2. The National Development Council
3. The Union Ministry of Rural Development
4. The Union Ministry of Urban Development
5. The Parliament

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
trapAnalysis:
Only the National Development Council (NDC) and Parliament are directly associated with 'Planning' in India: NDC — was the apex body that approved Five-Year Plans. It included the PM, all CMs, members of Planning Commission, and key Cabinet ministers. It was the highest decision-making body for planning. Parliament — approved the Plan and the budgetary allocation for it. Plans had no legal force until Parliament sanctioned the funds. Why others are excluded: Finance Commission (Art. 280) — deals with distribution of tax revenues between Centre and States. It's a constitutional body for fiscal transfers, NOT planning. Ministries of Rural/Urban Development — they are implementing agencies that execute plans, not bodies that formulate plans. The question asks about institutions associated with planning formulation, not implementation.

(Ref: Laxmikanth)

subject: Economy
stem:
What is/are the facility/facilities the beneficiaries can get from the services of Business Correspondent (Bank Saathi) in branchless areas ?

1. It enables the beneficiaries to draw their subsidies and social security benefits in their villages
2. It enables the beneficiaries in the rural areas to make deposits and withdrawals

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
trapAnalysis:
Business Correspondents (BCs), also called 'Bank Saathi,' are agents appointed by banks to provide basic banking services in remote villages where opening a full bank branch is not viable. They can do BOTH:

(1) Help villagers receive government subsidies and social security payments (like MGNREGA wages, pensions) directly.

(2) Accept deposits and process withdrawals. BCs were a key part of financial inclusion schemes like Swabhimaan. Think of them as mini mobile bank counters in branchless areas.

subject: Science
stem:
A Brief Account of Evolution

 About 2000 million years ago (mya) the first cellular forms of life appeared on earth. The mechanism of how non-cellular aggregates of giant macromolecules could evolve into cells with membranous envelop is not known. Some of these cells had the ability to release O2. The reaction could have been similar to the light reaction in photosynthesis where water is split with the help of solar energy captured and channelized by appropriate light harvesting pigments. Slowly single-celled organisms became multi-cellular life forms. By the time of 500 mya, invertebrates were formed and active. Jawless fish probably evolved around 350 mya. Sea weeds and few plants existed probably around 320 mya.

www.pmfias.com http://www.youtube.com/c/PoorMansFriend www.pmfias.com We are told that the first organisms that invaded land were plants. They were widespread on land when animals invaded land. Fish with stout and strong fins could move on land and go back to water. This was about 350 mya. These animals called lobefins evolved into the first amphibians that lived on both land and water. These were ancestors of modern day frogs and salamanders. The amphibians evolved into reptiles. They lay thick-shelled eggs which do not dry up in sun unlike those of amphibians. Again we only see their modern day descendents, the turtles, tortoises and crocodiles. In the next 200 million years or so, reptiles of different shapes and sizes dominated on earth. Giant ferns (pteridophytes) were present along with reptiles but they all fell to form coal deposits slowly. Some of these land reptiles went back into water to evolve into fish like reptiles probably 200 mya (e.g. Ichthyosaurs). The land reptiles were, of course, the dinosaurs. The biggest of them, i.e., Tyrannosaurus rex was about 20 feet in height and had huge fearsome dagger like teeth. About 65 mya, the dinosaurs suddenly disappeared from the earth. We do not know the true reason. Some say climatic changes killed them. Some say most of them evolved into birds. The truth may live in between. Small sized reptiles of that era still exist today. The first mammals were like shrews. Their fossils are small sized. Mammals were viviparous and protected their unborn young inside the mother s body. Mammals were more intelligent in sensing and avoiding danger at least. When reptiles came down mammals took over this earth. T here were in South America mammals resembling horse, hippopotamus, bear, rabbit, etc. Due to continental drift, when South America joined North America, these animals were overridden by North American fauna. Due to the same continental drift pouched mammals of Australia survived because of lack of competition from any other mammal. Q2. With reference to the evolution of living organisms, which one of the following sequences is correct? [2009]
options: (d) Frog-Crab-Prawn Answer: Evolution == Single cellular Multicellular Fishes Amphibians Reptiles
